summary: SDK sidecar keepalive trickle results in suppressed final chunk for long-running SSE sessions
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that long-running SSE streams from our hosted endpoint sometimes arrive to their client with all content except the final concluding chunk. Impact: Final sentence or closing JSON metadata is missing in 1-3% of sessions for a specific mobile app version, causing truncated completions and downstream UI to show a perpetual 'typing' indicator. Environment: Dedicated customer (Acme Retail) using Redwood hosted API via the mobile SDK v1.8.3 that runs a local sidecar process to multiplex network activity on flaky mobile connections.

Observed behavior differs from previous SSE truncation tickets because the server completes generation and emits the end event (visible in backend logs), but the client never receives the terminal chunk in a subset of reconnect/resume scenarios.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Install Acme mobile app with SDK v1.8.3 and enable sidecar multiplexing.
2) Start a long-running chat generation (~200-400 tokens) via SSE in us-east region.
3) Simulate intermittent network by toggling cellular data off/on twice quickly (to provoke socket handoff).
4) Observe stream resume; in affected runs the last 'end' event and final JSON metadata never arrive in the app while server logs show event emitted.
logs:
Backend excerpt (stream-id=stream-9a4f): 
[2026-03-05T08:12:14Z] generation.complete event emitted seq=0 end=true metadata={duration_ms:3214} 
Proxy/LB logs show FIN from client-side path at 08:12:14.108 and new connection at 08:12:14.210.
App-side sdk log snippet: 
[08:12:14.205] sidecar: keepalive: sent incremental probe (12 bytes)
[08:12:14.208] sdk: resumed SSE session, last_seq=0
[08:12:14.300] sdk: no terminal event received - session closed by app after timeout.
Packets captured at edge indicate a pattern of interleaved tiny keepalive writes during the TCP handoff window.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: When the mobile sidecar emits very small keepalive writes during connection handoff, some ALB/proxy implementations coalesce or reorder micro-frames and the final zero-length termination marker (or small JSON payload) from server is merged with a client probe in a way that the server-side connection close race drops the packet. We reproduced locally by injecting 8-16B client-side writes during an h2->h1 fallback; reproduced ~2/50 runs.
Findings:
- Server runtime always queues and sends final event; logs confirm flush.
- Edge (customer-dedicated ALB) behavior changes when client sends a write within 40-120ms of server final chunk.
- SDK sidecar v1.8.3 intentionally batches keepalives as tiny writes (to reduce wakeups); this pattern increases the race window.
- Workaround trial: disabling sidecar keepalive batching prevents truncation in reproduced cases.
Related: INT-1122 flagged an ALB keepalive coalescing regression; added as linked issue for infra follow-up.
comments: 2026-03-05 - Support (Ava Chen): Customer reports truncated final chunk in ~1.7% of long SSEs. Provided initial request id and stream ids.

2026-03-05 - SRE (Liam Patel): Collected edge/rt logs and packet captures; initial hypothesis: proxy coalescing with client-side micro-writes. Asked customer to enable SDK debug logging and to try a short test with keepalive disabled.

2026-03-06 - Customer (Acme Mobile Eng): We toggled sidecar keepalive batching off and ran 1000 sessions; observed 0 truncations in that run. Re-enabled for subsequent tests and saw truncations return. Shared logs and a capture of client probes.

2026-03-06 - Infra (Nina Gomez): Noted an ALB change last month that altered small-write coalescing behavior; opened INT-1122 to investigate config. Will test with stricter Nagle settings and TCP_NODELAY variants.
2026-03-07 - Support (Liam Patel): Proposed two short-term mitigations and a long-term fix. Posted steps below. Customer accepted mitigation A and is running validation.
2026-03-07 - Customer (Acme Mobile Eng): Applying mitigation A now, will report back after 24h of traffic.
proposed_workarounds:
A) On customer SDK side: disable keepalive micro-batching (SDK config: sidecar.keepalive.batching=false) — immediate and low-risk.
B) On server/edge: add a 50ms grace flush after emitting terminal chunk at edge layer to allow in-flight client writes to settle (requires infra change).
C) Client-level: extend resume wait timeout to tolerate late arrival of terminal chunk while keeping UI tolerant.
Customer accepted A for now.
resolution: In progress: Customer applied SDK config change disabling keepalive batching and reported initial validation with no truncations in 24h sample. Infra team (INT-1122) to validate ALB behavior; plan is to add a conservative 50ms flush on the dedicated ALB for long-lived SSE endpoints if we cannot tune the ALB. Follow-up actions: schedule release notes for SDK v1.8.4 documenting recommended default for sidecar batching and include a mitigation flag in hosted console for dedicated customers.
next_steps:
1) Monitor Acme's traffic for 72h post-mitigation and collect metrics (support will follow up).
2) Infra to run controlled ALB small-write coalescing test and update INT-1122 with findings.
3) Ship SDK patch v1.8.4 with keepalive.batching default=false and add telemetry to detect suppressed terminal events.
4) If infra fix is not feasible, implement server-side 50ms flush for SSE final frames behind a feature flag for dedicated clusters.
